sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who is calling, what does the agent resolve, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Converts calls a day into minutes, concurrency and turns a month
Defines resolved so that hang-ups and callbacks do not count
Estimates the human cost saved at the target resolution rate
Limits the first scope to a few high-volume intents

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the media and control path from a phone call to a reply and to a human.
criteria: Connects both legacy telephony platforms to one media path
Separates turn detection, speech to text, the model and text to speech as streaming stages
Routes payments to a PCI-compliant service outside the agent
Includes a warm handoff path back to the human queue with context

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What does the agent read, and which rules are data rather than prompt text?
criteria: Reads bookings live from the passenger service system
Keeps waiver and fare rules as a versioned rule table
Uses approved local-language policy text rather than live translation

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How is audio processed so each stage starts before the last ends?
criteria: Streams model output to TTS sentence by sentence
Detects language from the dialled number and the first seconds of speech
Stops ASR and recording during card payment by system control

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: Which models answer which turns, and what does it cost?
criteria: Lists cost levers in order with a monthly saving each, using the given prices
Uses a small fast model by default with the larger one chosen by workflow state
Triggers handoff on conditions written in code

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What is remembered, and how does barge-in affect it?
criteria: Truncates the assistant turn to the words actually played on barge-in
Keeps call state per region
Avoids voice biometrics or justifies them against special-category data rules

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: Which tools exist, and where are money limits enforced?
criteria: Enforces fare and waiver limits inside the rebooking tool
Uses idempotency keys on rebooking
Returns only a token from payment, never card data

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: Where do the 800 ms go, and what happens on a slow tool call?
criteria: Gives a stage latency budget under 800 ms at p95
Plays a filler when a tool call is slow so silence stays short
Describes barge-in detection with echo cancellation and a stop time
Keeps the loop in the caller's region

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached, and why does speech caching matter most?
criteria: Prices TTS per character and caches fixed phrases with the saving stated
Never caches personalized audio
Caches shared flight status briefly during disruption

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: What is stored where, how much, and what does the whole system cost?
criteria: Sizes recording storage from minutes a month and bytes a minute
Sizes ASR GPUs from peak concurrent streams with a stated per-GPU assumption
Gives a monthly total against the $400k budget with non-model prices labeled as assumed
Sets recording retention with a purpose

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does the caller hear, and what does the human receive?
criteria: Keeps spoken turns short
Reads confirmations back from tool results and sends them in writing
Attaches a structured summary to every handoff

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: Which legal and safety rules apply, and how are they enforced?
criteria: Discloses AI use and recording, with an opt-out
Requires stronger verification before changes than before reads
Keeps audio and transcripts in the entity's region with any transfer basis set per entity in code
Keeps card data out of the agent, transcripts and TTS

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: How do you prove the agent resolves calls well in every language?
criteria: Uses a holdout to measure resolution and CSAT
Reports metrics per language
Computes cost per resolved call against the human cost

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks on a live call, and what does the caller experience?
criteria: Falls back to a human transfer rather than silence
Covers a disruption surge with autoscaling and callbacks
Detects a degraded language from QA metrics and routes it to humans

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: How do you roll out 12 languages in 12 months?
criteria: Starts with one intent in one language
Launches languages in waves with QA calibration per language
Load-tests the disruption peak before full launch
